title: Desktop shell: desk, dock, extended desktop, Windows theme, Sticky Apps
summary: The desktop shell is among the most carefully engineered parts of the tree: one byte per desktop item ([desk_zslot]) reconciled by one liveness-only routine (desk_reflow), a cell drawn exactly once into the damage region by composed 1bpp bands, a dock that diffs tile keys and XORs self-inverse marks, and five on-demand modules (DOCK, WIN95, EXTD, STIKMENU and DESK) that keep decision code on disk with two principled hook shapes and a zero-resident-shim far-frame trick. Hostile input (SYSTEM.CFG trailer, .LNK, package link records) is bounded at each door. The weak spots are lifetime and target cost rather than drawing correctness: the Sticky App library's lifetime is keyed on a proxy (IF_DESK) instead of on who bound it, which is a latent use-after-free; every desktop gesture and every Sticky Apps menu press loads and drops a module, which the shell's own comments call too slow elsewhere; OSAPI_DESK_ITEM's remove is keyed by a zone that is not an identity, forcing WIN16 to probe; and the dock painter exists twice in source (and the two copies have already diverged beyond their geometry). Nothing needs an ABI break; the one ABI-shaped weakness has an additive fix. A long tail of comments and SPEC text still describes designs from before kernel size passes 12-14 and before SPEC 110.15 (held-until-restart, 1 KB claims, dkf_apply, wm_land_fit, desk_svflag), recorded below. [Verified 2026-11-08: 10 findings confirmed, 4 corrected, none refuted, 1 low left unchecked; 34 of the 39 structured doc mismatches confirmed, 4 more fixes added.]

strengths.title: One table, one reconciler for every desktop item
strengths.why: desk_reflow is told nothing about events and recomputes placement from liveness, posting exactly the cells that changed; mount, unmount, driver attach, shape change and a damaged SYSTEM.CFG pin block are all one call. The model to copy for any other placement problem.

strengths.title: Every pixel once, by construction
strengths.why: desk_col/desk_cap compose picture column and caption in RAM and put each down with one gfx_blit1, ground drawn round them; desk_zones_r_x draws cells into wm_dmg_gray's region with a counted overflow bound rather than an optimistic subtraction.

strengths.title: Dock tile key diff with self-inverse marks and a race-proof damage span
strengths.why: A focus change costs one gfx_xor_rect, never an erase-and-rebuild; the span is its own flag via the 07FFFh..08000h sentinel and the exchange is bracketed pushf/cli/popf so a concurrent force cannot be lost.

strengths.title: Two principled module hook shapes
strengths.why: Where the absent answer is a kernel body, a vector table rests on it and the module writes both halves (dkv, thv); where it is a refusal, calls go straight at mod_fp slots resting on mod_gone (EXTD, DESK, STIKMENU). No dispatcher, no resident second copy; EXTD's [vid_ndisp]>1-only-while-mounted invariant is kept by construction in EXF_SYNC.

strengths.title: Hand-built far frame onto cw_kretf
strengths.why: A module reaches any near kernel routine with zero resident shim (dkk_*, EXK/WNK/SMK); Mac trap glue and Win16 thunks needed a resident stub per entry.

strengths.title: Hostile bytes bounded at the door
strengths.why: ovl_sc_load terminates every string and frees rows with impossible kinds/volumes; sc_m_add re-stamps the picture header and forbids a forged Sticky mark; lnk_open bounds the volume, forces the NUL and bounds link chains by remaining stack.

strengths.title: Lifetime details that are easy to get wrong, got right
strengths.why: desk_need saves the outer drv_vol pair across a nested bracket; desk_drop_x counts unpublished records; stik_boot re-reads [sc_seg] after a load may compact.

strengths.title: Layouts asserted rather than trusted
strengths.why: DSV_R_SIZE, SC record tiling, ICO_BSTR, DKXPAD pad positions, stm_ctab/stm_atab order and the dword zone mask all fail the build if they drift.

findings.title: The Sticky App library can be freed under a widget that has bound it
findings.detail: DESK.DRV (which carries the shared Sticky App library) is dropped when no inst_tab record carries IF_DESK. Loader step 9 calls desk_drop_x (which clears the record's IF_DESK) for any launch whose returned window is not WF_DESK. A STIK_LIB widget has already bound the library by then: stik_load asks LIB and writes the library segment into every far pointer of stik_le. The library is built STIK_DESKONLY, under which stik_made issues MAKE and ignores its CF. So any MAKE refusal returns a titled window, step 9 drops DESK.DRV (if this is the only widget), and the next call far [stik_le+...] jumps into a freed heap claim. Every MAKE precondition holds for a correct package today, so it is latent, but the failure mode is a wild far call. The drop rule uses 'has a desk window' as a proxy for 'holds pointers into the library'.
evidence: kernel/loader.inc:1458-1466 step 9 drops for a non-WF_DESK window
apps/os88stikc.inc:152-176 stik_load binds LIB into stik_le
apps/stiklib.asm:28 STIK_DESKONLY forced in the library
apps/os88stik.inc:962-966 MAKE's CF ignored under STIK_DESKONLY
findings.recommendation: Cheapest: the library's stik_made refuses the launch when MAKE refuses (module bytes only). Right model: the LIB verb sets an IF_LIB bit (I_FLAGS bit 3 is free) on [ld_rec], desk_drop_x's scan tests IF_DESK|IF_LIB, and only the record's free (inst_alloc zeroes it) clears it - library lifetime by binder, as AmigaOS OpenLibrary/CloseLibrary.
findings.bytes_est: (a) +4..+6 DESK.DRV, 0 resident; (b) 0 resident .cold (the test immediate changes), +6 DESK.DRV
findings.prior_art: AmigaOS libraries: lib_OpenCnt governs expunge; a library is never freed on a proxy condition.
findings.verify_note: Re-read: desk_drop_x clears the passed record's IF_DESK and drops MOD_DESK when no record has it; step 9 calls it for any non-WF_DESK window; stik_load binds DX into every stik_le far pointer before STKE_LOAD; under STIK_DESKONLY stik_made's MAKE has no jnc/CF handling (os88stik.inc:962-966); MAKE refuses on six tests (deskmod.inc:239-258). Not in ABI-BREAK-LIST or KERNEL-BYTE-QUEUE. The library banner (deskmod.inc:369-375) and SPEC 110.15 still say 'held until the restart ... never freed under a caller', which is what the drop rule broke; those comments are fixed below.

findings.title: Interactive shell paths load and drop modules the shell itself calls too slow
findings.detail: desksc.inc moved the shortcut popup resident because 'an XT pays 2-3 s to load an image, which is a menu that does not come up', yet sc_modcall loads and drops MOD_SETS (CTRL.DRV's 3,180-byte settings core, MODS_SIZE) for every drag, delete, new shortcut and package link unless a Control Panel is already open; every press of the Sticky Apps cell loads STIKMENU.DRV (7,876-byte image, an 8 KB claim) and rescans STIKAPPS\ then drops it; and WIN16's DeleteGroup probes up to W16PG_SCN (15) zones with OSAPI_DESK_ITEM remove, each probe a sc_modcall load and drop. SPEC 110.12 prices the menu's load at ~2-3 calls, about a second, before the panel is drawn.
findings.recommendation: Give the interactive modules a third lifetime: DISCARDABLE - kept after use as a low-priority purgeable claim and shed by mem_claim's shed-and-retry. Start with MOD_SETS and MOD_STIKM, both entered only from the UI task with no re-entry, so the per-module nesting count of ONDEMAND-PLAN 7.1 reduces to the existing loaded row plus a purge tag. A second visit on a roomy machine then costs no disk.
findings.bytes_est: +40..+80 resident (mod_drop's discard arm, the purge tag) for the two; the full HEAP-UNPIN piece B is +215..+240 resident
findings.prior_art: Windows 3.0/3.1 DISCARDABLE code segments (reloaded from the EXE only when actually discarded); Mac Resource Manager purgeable resources.
findings.listed_as: docs/plans/completed/ONDEMAND-PLAN.md 7.2; docs/plans/HEAP-UNPIN-PLAN.md piece B; SPEC 110.12 'No cache of the scan'
findings.verify_note: Real. Corrected the MOD_SETS size: MODS_SIZE = mods_end - $$ = 0xC6C = 3,180 bytes (build/kernel.map), not 2,206; and SPEC 110.12's price is '~2-3 calls, about a second, before the panel is drawn' (the load), not a 'drop'. sc_modcall uses the open panel's copy when MOD_CTRL is live (desksc.inc:437-458). Both plan listings exist (ONDEMAND-PLAN 7.2, HEAP-UNPIN piece B at ~215-240).

findings.title: OSAPI_DESK_ITEM remove is keyed by a zone that the API says is not an identity
findings.detail: A package removes 'the link in zone AH, ES:SI = the record it added', and sc_m_pdel must re-verify volume and path because zones are reused and renumbered at boot. A caller that did not keep the zone must probe, which WIN16 does over every shortcut zone, each probe a module load. The Sticky App row already has the right shape: AH = 0xFF finds by name.
findings.recommendation: Additive now: AH = 0FEh 'the row whose volume and path are this record's', walking rows with sc_m_same; WIN16 makes one call. At the next flag day, re-contract remove to be by record always and drop the zone argument.
findings.bytes_est: +~12 CTRL.DRV (.modc), 0 resident; WIN16 -~12 package; flag-day follow-on -~6 resident .cold (desk.inc:2283-2284)
findings.prior_art: Win95 shell links and Mac aliases identify by path/ID, never by a screen slot.
findings.verify_note: osapi_desk_item_x .pdel passes any AH >= DESK_SC0 (0FFh included) straight to sc_modcall (desk.inc:2275-2284); sc_m_dfind only matches SC_STIK rows, so WIN16's group link cannot use 0FFh; w16pg_delgrp loops W16PG_SC0..+15 with a module load per probe. sc_m_same already exists to reuse. Not listed in the ABI or byte queues.

findings.title: The dock painter is hand-copied into DOCK.DRV
findings.detail: db_paint/db_key/db_tile_rect/db_draw_tile/db_click/db_rclick and dkx_paint/dkx_key/dkx_tile_rect/dkx_draw_tile/dkx_click/dkx_rclick are the same algorithm written twice, prose invariants included (one-exit, dock_drew wrap, the xchg bracket). The copies have already diverged beyond their geometry source - dkx_paint banks gfx_hole/wm_clip_n round the paint and clears dock_drew while the strip is open, and the two push their registers differently (kent_di vs six pushes) - and the comments drifted together ('the five pops at the bottom' in both, where the exits pop seven and nine). The tree's own idiom for this is a macro assembled per image (DESK_ROWCALC, DOCK_GEOM, DOCK_APPLY, EXF_SYNC).
evidence: kernel/dockmod.inc:524-533, :746-751 (the module-only hole/region and dock_up arms)
findings.recommendation: One DOCK_PAINT macro parameterised on the geometry source (immediates DOCK_X0/DOCK_STEP for the basic strip, [cs:dock_a0]/[cs:dock_astep] and dkx_swap_side in the module) plus %if arms for the module-only hole/region bank and the open-strip CF, so a fix lands once.
findings.bytes_est: 0 if each expansion keeps today's instructions (the arms must reproduce the divergences)
findings.verify_note: Real duplication, but the reviewer understated the divergence: dkx_paint has a hole/region bank and an open-strip CF clear that db_paint lacks, and different prologue encodings, so a single macro needs several %if arms, and '0 bytes' holds only if those reproduce today's code. Severity medium -> low: a maintenance risk, no defect.

findings.title: Three textual copies of the far-frame helper
findings.detail: exk_go, wnk_go and smk_go are the same 17 source lines (16 instructions and the PUSH_KCODE macro), instruction for instruction; dockmod's dkk_* is the per-routine form. Each image must carry its own, but they should share source.
findings.recommendation: One %macro MODK_GO in kernel/mod.inc, expanded per image.
findings.verify_note: The three bodies are identical (wnk_go and smk_go's banners say so). Count is 17 source lines, not '19 instructions' - detail adjusted.

findings.title: Locator File menu item 1 is poked by raw offset from five sites
findings.detail: desk_select, desk_unsel_x, sc_rclick_x (twice) and sc_m_del address the Remove Shortcut item as menu_items_file+2; the table's own comment names the wrong writer (ui_loc_gate, which writes item 0).
findings.recommendation: MENU_FILE_REM equ menu_items_file + 2 beside the table with an %if MENU_FILE_N != 2 guard, used at every site; fix the comment.
findings.verify_note: Five sites confirmed (desk_select, desk_unsel_x, sc_rclick_x x2, sc_m_del); ui_loc_gate writes [menu_items_file] (item 0). Comment fixed below.

findings.title: STIKMENU.DRV writes the kernel's service-item record
findings.detail: With no driver registered, More Sticky Apps copies THEWIRE.O88 and The Wire into desk_svc_file/desk_svc_name so ui_svc_open can be reused, leaving a half-written service record in resident .bss for the session and making desk_svc_rec a two-writer structure whose second writer is a module.
findings.recommendation: Hand ui_svc_open the file and name as inputs, or launch by name from the module as stm_a_launch already does.
findings.verify_note: stm_a_more copies DSV_FILEMAX and DSV_NAMEMAX bytes into desk_svc_file/desk_svc_name when [desk_svc_seg] = 0, then calls cw_ui_svc_open. Harmless while desk_svc_seg stays 0 (nothing else reads the strings then), so low is right.

findings.title: Boot reader keeps up to 1 KB more shortcut claim than the rows need
findings.detail: ovl_sc_load claims the whole SYSTEM.CFG (head + rows + placed cells + footer) in KB as the shortcut table and moves rows to its base but never shrinks it; the claim stays file-sized until the first add or delete regrows it through sc_m_kb. With CFG_FBUF about 140 bytes, 7, 8 or 15 rows cross a KB boundary: 2 KB for 1 KB of rows, 3 for 2. Movable, so not a wall, but heap held for the session.
evidence: kernel/desksc.inc:1227-1272 sc_m_kb is the only resize
findings.recommendation: mem_regrow to ceil(rows/8) KB after the row move, in .boot2 (or .cfx if the blob has no room).
findings.verify_note: Behaviour confirmed (claim = ceil(file/1024) KB at desksc.inc:1767-1771; nothing in ovl_sc_load resizes; sc_m_row/sc_m_kb are the only resizes). Kind bug -> weakness: nothing malfunctions, it is heap held; the claim is MOVABLE (sc_reloc). ovl_sc_load is in .boot2 (desksc.inc:1706).

findings.title: Every damage pass recomputes every shown cell's rect with div and two muls
findings.detail: desk_dmg_zones_x calls desk_cell_rect -> desk_cell_xy (cbw/cwd/div word, mul bx, mul word) and a far cw_wm_dmg_hit for every shown zone on every window move, close or raise: ~700 cycles (~150 us) per shown zone, ~0.9 ms for six, though most damage never reaches the cell columns.
findings.recommendation: One early-out of the damage rect against the grid's x extent, a word derived in DESK_GRID, before the walk.
findings.verify_note: desk_cell_xy is div word + two muls (8088: ~150 + 2x~120 cycles) plus calls and the far dmg_hit; the per-zone estimate is plausible. Predicted, not measured.

findings.title: WIN95.DRV phases button art one bit at a time
findings.detail: wn_blit shifts each 16-bit art row into three bytes with shr ax,1/rcr bp,1/loop per bit: up to 7 x ~21 cycles per row, 13 rows, three buttons and the grip - about 0.5-1 ms CPU per title bar on the 8088 under the Windows theme.
findings.recommendation: shr ax,cl for the two bytes and a shl by 8-cl of a copy of the low byte for the spill.
findings.verify_note: The per-bit loop is at winmod.inc:472-475; arithmetic is plausible (predicted).

findings.title: Basic dock_geom only works at boot or with CTRL.DRV loaded
findings.detail: dkb_geom runs the blob's copy while [spl_fseg] is set and otherwise far-calls CTRL.DRV's CPE_DOCK_GEOM. Every caller today is the boot, DOCK_APPLY or the Display page, so it holds; a future caller outside the panel gets mod_gone's CF=1 and no geometry, silently.
findings.recommendation: State the invariant in dkb_geom's banner, or fall back to dkb_band on CF=1.
findings.verify_note: dkb_geom: `cmp [spl_fseg],0 / je .panel / SPLGATE1 ovl_dock_geom` else `call far [CPFP+CPE_DOCK_GEOM*4]`; callers are the VSW_SWITCH/VSW_DISP expansions (blob, CTRL.DRV), DOCK_APPLY's reflow and vid_init. With DOCK.DRV mounted the slot is dkx_geom, so only the basic arm is exposed.

findings.title: A driver's service record is half-sanitised
findings.detail: osapi_desk_item_x force-terminates only the caption; the 13-byte launch file and 12-byte header name are copied as given and later read as NUL strings. Drivers are trusted and the SDK marks both fields 'NUL' (the driver's obligation); the SDK's 'Both strings are terminated by the kernel' sits in the package's paragraph and means the package record's path and caption, which sc_m_add does terminate.
findings.recommendation: Optional: terminate the file and name too, for symmetry with the caption.
findings.verify_note: The code half is confirmed (only desk_svc_cap+DSV_CAPMAX-1 is forced). The SDK-contradiction half is refuted: 'Both strings' follows the package record and its remove clause (two strings: path, caption) and the driver's three are each documented NUL. Recommendation reduced; the proposed os88api.inc:1446 doc fix is dropped.

findings.title: desk_reflow is O(cells x zones) per placement
findings.detail: desk_free calls desk_owner (a 24-entry scan) for each cell from 0, and pass 2 calls it per item; a screen-shape reflow re-places every flowing item. Tens of ms on the XT at worst, once per display switch.
findings.recommendation: An occupancy bitmap built once per reflow (desk_cdirty's shape) would make it linear; not worth ~30 resident bytes for a mount-rate path.
findings.verify_note: Spot-checked: desk_free loops cells calling desk_owner, which scans DESK_NZ bytes.

findings.title: kern_small still draws a desktop cell two and three times
findings.detail: kern_small's desk_draw_zone fills the whole zone with ground, draws the icon over it, fills a white caption rect over the ground and then an opaque font_run over the white: caption band written three times, picture twice, on the slowest machine. SPEC 26.9.9 records kern_big's fix as kern_big-only by design.
findings.recommendation: A cheaper partial (ground above the caption band and two side strips) costs ~+2 primitive calls and ~+20 resident bytes; take a flicker measurement before deciding.
findings.verify_note: Spot-checked: cw_thm_desk over desk_rect_ax, cw_icon_draw_ix, ct_cw_gfx_fill white, then font_run_x.

findings.title: Windows title bar ground is filled under its buttons and caption
findings.detail: wn_title fills the whole bar and then the button bands and opaque caption land on it, writing ~3x15x13 button pixels and the caption cells twice per title paint. SPEC 76.14.3 records the decision; logged against PERFORMANCE rule 2.
findings.recommendation: If the theme ever becomes a default, compose the bar into one band (the composed-bar knob) instead of splitting fills.
findings.verify_note: Low, recorded decision; only the fill/buttons/font_run order was glanced at, not the SPEC 76.14.3 reasoning.

; dock_apply - the SETTING moved: geometry, drive column, windows, strip
; in:  [dock_cfg] already written; gfx lock held by the caller, or at boot
; out: nothing (all registers preserved). THE CALLER OWES THE REPAINT, which
;      is vid_switch's own contract: the Control Panel posts [cp_dirty]
;
; SPEC.md 30.5. wm_refit moves every window back inside the new band, and the
; raise caches go because a window that did not move can have had the strip
; stand up or lie down behind it.
doc_fixes.new_text:
; dkx_paint - db_paint (dock.inc) on any edge: the rule and white field when
;             the damage span says they are owed, then every tile whose key moved
; in:  nothing (caller holds the gfx lock)
; out: CF = 1 if any pixel was drawn, CF = 0 if the strip was already right -
;      and CF = 0 while the strip is OPEN, which damages no window. All
;      registers preserved; [gfx_color], [gfx_hole] and [wm_clip_n] restored.
doc_fixes.why: The banner over dkx_paint (dockmod.inc:505) is a stale copy of dock_apply's; DOCK_APPLY lives in dock.inc:287-340 and answers CF. dkx_paint's CF and the dock_up clear are at dockmod.inc:743-762.
